title: csm-orchestrate approach fidelity and residual limitations: pass 1

tldr.content: Pass 1 verdict: the implementation is a substantially faithful, contract-heavy controller prototype, not a production-complete outer loop. The six original findings are largely addressed, but phase-review independence, bounded remediation, insertion semantics, exact approval binding, and host-backed durability remain gaps.

executiveSummary.content:
The review compared the agreed grill approach with commit d2fd905, local tests, packaged mirrors, and current standards. The implementation now has JSON contracts, conditional routing, typed handoffs, bounded read-only scheduling, retry intent, durable receipt extensions, and fail-closed host review boundaries. The strongest residual risk is that repository tests can validate a synthetic host contract but cannot prove the external host actually provides reviewer isolation, approval authenticity, resolver integrity, or cross-process durability.

ask -> approach comparison -> source/test audit -> residual limitation analysis

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported: Canonical JSON approach phases compile to immutable ordered phases and declared capability routes [R1][R2].
K2. partially-supported: Requirement and signal IDs prevent broad accidental acceptance, but caller-supplied evidence metadata is not substantive semantic entailment [R1][R3].
K3. partially-supported: Final review has a host-only provenance boundary, but phase-level adversarial callbacks can remain local [R1].
K4. partially-supported: Handoffs and bounded read-only scheduling exist, but external inputs, approvals, and concurrent recovery still depend on host/store semantics [R1][R4][R5].
K5. not-supported: Production readiness and outcome improvement are not demonstrated by synthetic tests [R4][R6].
K6. not-supported: Bounded remediation and requested insertion position are not fully enforced at runtime [R1].

detailSections.content:
Approach fidelity: the code matches the approach on canonical JSON, producer ownership, typed child lineage, approval-gated dispatch, separate technical/functional gates, final review, remediation lineage, and bounded read-only scheduling. It differs where the approach says every material delegated output receives independent adversarial review, every remediation loop is bounded, inserted phases preserve requested graph position, and approvals bind exact artifact inputs.

Technical faults and functional gaps: the local review seam is structurally labeled but phase acceptance still permits it; remediation metadata is validated but budget consumption and insertion are incomplete; controller-level queues are not cross-process locks; approval consumption and host execution are external; and no production telemetry/evaluation proves accuracy, cost, latency, or human-correction outcomes.

Residual limitation solution direction: introduce an authenticated host protocol with signed reviewer and artifact attestations, a strongly consistent cursor/idempotency store, durable cancellation/reconciliation, exact approval request digests, and a deployment-like evaluation corpus with blinded adjudication and rollback thresholds.

recommendation.content: Do not widen autonomy or claim production readiness yet. Keep the controller fail-closed and address the host boundary as a separate integration surface: (1) require host-issued signed review attestations and exact request/approval binding; (2) use compare-and-set/fencing semantics for cursor, terminal, and idempotency records; (3) make remediation budget and insertion position executable invariants; (4) add trace/metric correlation and a held-out baseline evaluation before any production canary. This preserves the original outer-loop design rather than replacing it with a new workflow engine.

unverifiedClaims.content: Production reviewer isolation, approval authenticity, artifact authorship, resolver trust, cross-process cursor linearizability, late side-effect behavior after timeout, and real cancellation semantics remain unverified. Semantic entailment is only structurally represented: a hostile producer may still assert a matching signal unless an independent validator evaluates the signal against the artifact. Accuracy, latency, cost, recovery, and human-correction improvement have no empirical evidence.

references.content: Local source claims are pinned to GitHub commit d2fd905. External references cover durable execution, provenance, remote attestation, authorization, retries, and SLO/evaluation design.

processAppendix.content: Pass 1 used four independent read-only research tracks: approach fidelity, technical/security audit, host-boundary limitations, and operability/evaluation. Sources were hybrid local repository inspection plus current authoritative web retrieval. No repository code was changed. This is pass 1 input for a second challenge pass and a final adversarial pass.

claims.statement: The implementation compiles canonical JSON approach phases into immutable ordered runtime phases and validates the complete capability manifest.
Requirement and acceptance-signal binding is stronger than the previous implementation but does not prove the substance of an artifact satisfies the signal.
Final review has a host-backed token boundary, while phase-level adversarial review can still use the local review seam.
Declared upstream handoffs and bounded read-only scheduling are implemented, but their durability and host enforcement are external conditions.
Remediation lineage is retained, but runtime budget consumption and requested insertion position are not fully executable invariants.
A process-local write queue and in-memory idempotency map do not establish cross-process durable execution semantics.
Production readiness and improvement in correctness, latency, cost, recovery, or human correction are not established without deployment-like measurement and independent adjudication.
The safest way to address the residual limitations is to strengthen the external host, attestation, storage, telemetry, and evaluation boundaries while preserving the controller architecture.
